vercel:usage-days-diagnostic.note: One fixed-shape terminal diagnostic per private-days request in provider-managed Vercel runtime logs. r2:canonical-contribution-bodies.note: Content-addressed canonical batch bodies under usage-contributions/v3 in the existing private STAGING binding. Reservation charges possible immutable bytes before I/O; uncertain and abandoned bodies remain charged. Reclamation requires a separate qualified lifecycle operation.

service:canonical-contributions-v3.note: Nine exact device-authenticated upload/status/heads/abandon/full-batch-cancel/population/activation/migration/cancel-migration endpoints. Full-batch cancellation retains one metadata-only terminal fence for an absent frozen operation, consumes its next device sequence and empty canonical revision once, and dispatches no content-store write. Head reads use indexed bounded pages with exact account, generation, device, writer, population and canonical-revision correlation. Exact master, admission, stats and contributions flags are required. No flag is enabled by publication. Account transactions own enrollment, restore, generation and cutover authority.

r2:canonical-contribution-artifacts.note: Immutable correction-reference pages, roots and sealed legacy migration manifests. Canonical SQL commitment, never R2 presence, establishes publication. All possible artifact bytes are reserved before I/O and uncertain outcomes remain charged.

r2:canonical-contribution-index.note: Immutable account/generation-bound B+tree nodes. Durable step reservations bound cumulative possible writes at 4 GiB independently of canonical source budgets; exact retries never recharge. Published roots become queryable only by their committed SQL reference. Internal whole-key-space scans return at most 16 cells with authenticated key/ordinal continuations; semantic comparison reads at most two such pages per step, with no writes or publication authority. Physical reclamation remains disabled pending retention/recovery qualification.
r2:canonical-contribution-index.source: committed canonical contribution journal including verified sealed legacy references

worker:usage_contribution_projection_con.note: Bounded projection reservation and committed publication authority only; numeric cells live in immutable content storage. Shared limits are not additional allocations per table. Every possible write is charged before provider I/O; uncertainty stays charged. Retired cursor references expire 930000ms after replacement and are pruned only by explicit publication. Physical node deletion and recovery invalidation remain qualification-gated.

worker:usage_contribution_projection_pen.note: Bounded projection reservation and committed publication authority only; numeric cells live in immutable content storage. worker:usage_contribution_projection_pub.note: Bounded projection reservation and committed publication authority only; numeric cells live in immutable content storage. Shared limits are not additional allocations per table. Every possible write is charged before provider I/O; uncertainty stays charged. Retired cursor references expire 930000ms after replacement and are pruned only by explicit publication. Physical node deletion and recovery invalidation remain qualification-gated.

service:canonical-contribution-query.note: Dormant account-private indexed page endpoint. Exact master, stats, contributions, auth and private-read flags plus verified workload identity are required. Caller account assertions come from the authenticated coordinator. Every page pins a retained committed root and exposes source/snapshot lag; reads perform no DML or projection work.

worker:account_work.note: Two bounded work identities, retry budgets and independently versioned dispatch flights. One durable watchdog marks unresolved I/O awaiting settlement; neither yielding nor expiry releases restore custody. Completion persists its next wake before clearing the flight. No numeric content or unbounded queue. New canonical accounts only; physical deletion remains gated by account recovery qualification.

service:canonical-contribution-cell-scru.note: Trusted coordinator read-only diagnostic; no public route. Qualifies one cell relative to fresh V3 canonical SQL heads, with at most 16 heads, 16 source bodies and 7 index nodes; the 23 object reads and 18 MiB decoded budget exclude two namespace and two external restore-fence reads. One 30-second nonrenewable RPC deadline includes those authority checks. Legacy, larger and lagging accounts refuse explicitly. The fold is independent of projection deltas; no repair, checkpoint, quota, object or alarm write occurs. Logical read bounds do not attest physical storage, original source truth or whole-account correctness.

local:canonical-contribution-checkpoint.note: Inactive native V3 foundation; no command or transport route. One authenticated current/staged checkpoint and stable lock per account/device/generation owner across all populations. Exact current flight and last terminal body survive uncertainty; upload-to-cancel intent is durable before dispatch. Existing-only shared inspection performs no creation, promotion or sync. Explicit recovery verifies predecessor transitions and re-establishes durability before granting a borrowed flight capability. Never delete or overwrite checkpoint files to recover. Bounds describe logical payloads, not physical disk allocation; independent custody is still required to detect arbitrary older valid directory restores.

worker:usage_contribution_rebuild_jobs.note: Explicit diagnostic job identities, pinned canonical/publication roots, checked source and comparison cursors, idempotent step receipts and reserved scratch writes. Up to 16 lifetime jobs including terminals; IDs never restart and no physical job deletion is implemented. Scratch objects share the existing cumulative 4 GiB projection write budget; uncertain/aborted writes are not refunded. This control table grants no publication or repair authority. Schema13 is added only by trusted fenced begin; status is SELECT-only.

worker:usage_reclamation_ledger.note: Durable reclamation-ledger-v1: one row per candidate object keyed by (surface, key) with state recorded|held|deleting|reclaimed|refused, horizon, attempt and hold markers. Recording is idempotent and never deletes. The consuming job is disabled by default (AICHARTS_USAGE_RECLAMATION_ENABLED stays unset everywhere), creates the table only on an explicit flagged record, re-walks every reference inside the account transaction and deletes at most four quiescent, horizon-expired, unreferenced objects per step. Rows are never physically deleted; refused rows await operator review. Implemented, not live-qualified.

service:canonical-contribution-rebuild.note: Trusted foreground diagnostic with no public route or alarm class. One step processes at most 16 canonical heads, or compares two internal 16-cell pages. Actual source/index read and scratch-write counters are retained with the step. 1040 object reads/80 MiB decoded content cover source bodies plus separate bounded index planning and stage readback; comparison caps252 reads/64 MiB. These exclude external namespace/fence checks. One nonrenewable 30-second RPC deadline includes external authority I/O, while actual provider puts retain restore custody until settlement. A match is relative to retained canonical SQL authority, not original source truth or a recovery/cutover certificate.
